PositiveEm ~ a*Type
Type ~ b*Effect + c*Distin + d*SelfE + e*Projec + f*Relat
PositiveEm ~ g*Effect + h*Distin + i*SelfE + j*Proje + k*Relat

#indirect effects
ind_eff := b*g
ind_dis := c*h
ind_self := d*i
ind_pro:= e*j
ind_rel := f*k
'

nBoots <- 2000

#Fit the multigroup model with boostrap
fit <- sem(study1.mod,data=study1, group="Time", group.equal = c("loadings"), , bootstrap = nBoots)

#Output
summary(fit, standardized=TRUE, rsq=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
parameterEstimates(fit, boot.ci.type = "norm", standardized = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup Mediation SEM
parts: fit <- sem(study1.mod,data=study1, group="Time", group.equal = c("loadings"), , bootstrap = nBoots)
Your model does not have any factor loadings. This does not make any sense.
Is it possible that group.equal = c("loadings") is fixing the paths to be equal in path analysis?

You don't have factors, only observed variables.  Behind the scenes, lavaan creates a single indicator "factor" for each observed variable, simply because the LISREL representation of an SEM only has matrices of directed paths in which latent factors are predictors (Lambda has observed outcomes, Beta has latent outcomes).
Is this OK to compare models across groups with "loadings" or should I use something different?

You should explicitly add the constraints you want to add, so that you know what you are doing.  The group.equal= argument is a shortcut meant for easily adding measurement-invariance constraints, not for path analysis.  Read this page about using the same label to constrain parameters across groups to equality.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
